references.text: The spoils were divided among the warriors and the rest of the congregation, reflecting the same principle of sharing war booty with the brothers.
The warriors took spoils for themselves, including gold, silver, and other valuables, similar to the list of riches mentioned here.
David established a law that those who stayed behind with the equipment should share the spoils equally with those who went out to battle, the same principle that Joshua conveys.
Moses instructed the tribes on the east side of the Jordan to let their women, children, and livestock remain while the men crossed over to fight, promising to return to their property afterward.

Joshua reminded Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh that their women, children, and livestock should stay on the east side while they helped their brothers, and that they would return to their inheritance afterward.
It mentions wealth in the form of silver and gold, which are among the valuable items listed in Joshua's speech.
Jacob's sons took spoils including livestock and riches, similar to the categories of war booty mentioned in this passage.
